tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H18): TMA/bulk-staged depthwise conv (K1) with hardware zero padding, replacing LDG/LDGSTS staging. Step 0: try `nvidia-smi -lgc 1500` on the rented card once and record whether it works (if it does, use it for every timing in this session and say so in findings). Interleave r1-lib-cublaslt-fp16-v3fix as the control in the same container for every comparison (3 rounds). Step 1 (stage-only probe, 15 min): a kernel that only stages x into smem through a 4-stage mbarrier ring and touches nothing else. For W%4==0 rows (28,32,56,64,112) build a 3-D CUtensorMap over x as dims {W, H, B*C} fp32, box {WT+6 rounded up to a 16 B multiple, RT+6, 8 channels}, coordinates (w0-3, h0-3, c0); the TMA unit zero-fills out-of-bounds rows and columns. For 7x7, 14x14 and 449x7 rows the row stride (28/56/28 B) is not a 16 B multiple, so stage whole planes with 1-D cp.async.bulk: 4-channel groups (784 B for 7x7, 50288 B for 449x7) or one 14x14 plane (784 B), and pad by index math in smem (issue all copies before any wait). 2 CTAs/SM, 64-100 KB smem per CTA. Measure GB/s per SM cold (after the 2xL2 zero-fill) at 64,96,112,112, 8,320,32,32 and 1,96,56,56 against the current staging (148 us at 8,320; 9.5 us for the 64-channel band). Kill if under 40 GB/s per SM or not 2x faster than the current staging. Step 2: put the winning staging into K1 (conv math, weight prep, LN partial stats and fp16 d output unchanged from v3fix); keep the 1-warp/tall-tile dispatch for small shapes only if it still wins. Keep attributes only ever raised (portal-order constraint) and rebuild the tensor map on the host every call (pointers shift). Step 3: add clock64 + globaltimer stamps inside K1 at 1,192,28,28 to report how much of K1 is cycles vs ns (audit item). Step 4: run_tests 16/16 x 10 rounds and log per workload the max |err| and the count of elements beyond atol; report them in findings. Success: K1 cold at 1,96,56,56 <= 9 us (from 16.4), at 8,320,32,32 <= 30 us (from 61.4), at 64,96,112,112 <= 500 us (from 954); run_tests 16/16 with zero beyond-atol elements; projected score >= 0.62 (from 0.594) with v3fix interleaved as control. Refuted if: The stage-only TMA/bulk ring is less than 2x faster than the LDG staging at 8,320,32,32 or below 40 GB/s per SM at the largest (then the cost is halo redundancy / request pattern, not the instruction path, and conv work must move to fewer, taller tiles or tensor cores). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

Experiment E2 (tests H19): Flatten the cooperative kernel's latency chain: cross-barrier prefetch, in-CTA weight conversion at C<=384, per-image s_b publisher. Step 1 (audit, 20 min): add %globaltimer and clock64 stamps at each phase boundary and after each dependent wait (weight pass, conv loads, sumsq read, s_b read, W2 first stage) at 1,192,28,28, 2,768,7,7 and 8,384,14,14 (CTA medians). Build a loads-only stub (same loads and stores, MMA and conv FMAs removed) and record how much of the ~25 us above F is pure latency vs SM cycles. Step 2: issue every phase-2 operand (first W1 cp.async stages, the d tile, b1, u/c1 vectors) before grid.sync 1 so the barrier wait overlaps the loads; before grid.sync 2 prefetch the W2 K-slices and the x residual tile; after sync 2 only the s_b read remains. Keep every arrive in warps that have no loads in flight. Step 3: for C <= 384 drop the global weight pass: load fp32 W1/W2 tiles with cp.async into an fp32 staging stage, cvt.rn.f16x2 and STS into the fp16 ring inside the consuming CTA (row sums for the LN fold from the converted values); keep the global pass only at C=768. Step 4: replace the sumsq-atomics-then-reread round with a per-image last-arriver (counter in the torch.empty workspace, self-resetting) that computes and publishes s_b[4C]. Step 5: keep registers at 128 (check for spills; a PF-deep prefetch that spills is a dead end). Step 6: run_tests 16/16 x 10 rounds, interleaved with the parent, and log per workload the max |err| and the count beyond atol. Success: Rented, interleaved: 1,192,28,28 <= 22 us (from 29.7), 2,96,56,56 <= 30 (42.2), 4,192,28,28 <= 34 (47.2), 2,768,7,7 <= 40 (47.9), no row slower than the parent by more than 2%; projected score >= 0.60 (from 0.561). Refuted if: The loads-only stub shows less than 8 us of latency in the ~25 us of phases at 1,192,28,28 (then the lever is instruction count per phase, not round trips), or the cross-barrier prefetch spills and the S rows do not move. Experiment E3 (tests H20): One-barrier on-chip-hidden kernel for the C<=192 rows: smem hidden tile, bulk weight rings, red.add split-K GEMM2. Pivot: no clusters, no DSMEM. Step 1 (probe, 15 min): 148 CTAs (1/SM, cooperative launch) each cp.async.bulk-load 300 KB and 590 KB of fp32 from an L2-resident buffer through a 4-stage ring and convert to fp16 in smem; time under harness_time after the 2xL2 zero-fill and report GB/s per SM. Go if 300 KB takes <= 3 us; if above 6 us, use BN = C slices (more conv redundancy, half the ingest). Step 2 (kernel, dispatch:size, other rows routed to the lineage's existing paths so 16/16 passes): one cooperative launch, one grid.sync. Per-shape planner picks T tokens x BN hidden channels per CTA (tiles never straddle images; e.g. 1,192: 37 token tiles x 4 hidden blocks of 192; 1,96: BN=384 with ~21 tokens per CTA) so that conv x (4C/BN) / 148 + weight bytes(BN) / ingest rate + red.add M*C*4*(4C/BN) / 4.3 TB/s is minimised. Phase A, all loads issued at entry: the x halo patch for the CTA's tokens over all C channels, the W1 slice [BN x C] and W2 slice [C x BN] fp32 through the rings, converted to fp16 on the way into smem (no weight pass, no second barrier). Conv (register patches, plane fill with 16 loads issued before stores), LN per token (mean/rstd in fp32), mma.sync m16n8k16 GEMM1 (per-shape template, no runtime guard around HMMA), erf GELU, hidden tile [T x BN] fp16 kept in smem; per-(image, k) sumsq partials written to per-CTA slots in the torch.empty workspace (no atomics, no zeroing). CTAs of hidden block 0 write out = x + b2 with plain stores. grid.sync. Phase B: read the slots of the CTA's image (<= 60 KB from L2), mu_b and s_b, scale the smem hidden in place (h*s_b[k] + gb[k]), GEMM2 partial [T x C] over K = BN with the W2 slice, red.global.add.f32 into out (plain stores when BN = 4C). Step 3: run_tests 16/16 x 10 rounds; log per workload the max |err| and the count beyond atol; report the phase timeline (globaltimer) at 1,192 and 4,192. Success: Rented: 1,192,28,28 <= 18 us, 1,96,56,56 <= 16, 2,96,56,56 <= 20, 4,192,28,28 <= 24, 4,96,56,56 <= 26, 8,192,28,28 <= 32 (lineage B today: 30.9 / 28.3 / 42.2 / 47.2 / 62.5 / 66.1); 16/16 pass with zero beyond-atol elements. Refuted if: The bulk-ring ingest probe exceeds 6 us for 300 KB per SM, or the full kernel exceeds 25 us at 1,192,28,28 and 2,96,56,56 (then on-chip hidden has no edge over B's phases at S and lineage C is re-seeded from the tcgen05 family, H23, in r3).
